1.text: By them. Viz. the tongue and the lips, mentioned in the last verse of the foregoing chapter. Ch. --- We cannot resist of ourselves, and must therefore pray to God. W. --- We have need of a good master to correct our eagerness in speaking. C.

2.text: Ignorances, &c. That is, that the scourges and discipline of wisdom may restrain the ignorances, that is, the slips and offences which are usually committed by the tongue and the lips. Ch. --- The tongue is a restless evil. Jam. iii. 8.

3.text: Over me. The noblest motives are not always proposed first.

5.text: Eyes. God never makes such presents, but he permits us to fall in punishment of former transgressions. C. --- Coveting. Gr. "from thy servants all giant-like affection. Vain hopes and desires remove from me; and thou shalt possess him who wishes to serve thee without ceasing." Grabe. H.

6.text: Foolish, (infrunitæ) is used in this sense by Seneca. C. --- Greek has not this epithet. The title, "instruction of the mouth," follows, (H.) to v. 20. C.

10.text: Them. Gr. Alex. has only (9.) "swearing, (10.) and have not a custom of naming the Most High." Other editions have "the holy one." H. --- Rash and false oaths are forbidden. Jer. iv. Matt. v. W.

11.text: Sin. "No swearing is secure." S. Aug. --- Slaves were forced to confess the truth by torments; free-men took an oath; and priests gave their word. Plut. Prob.

13.text: Dissemble. Gr. "despise." He will be punished, at least, by God. C.

14.text: In vain. Without a design to execute, (Grot.) or through levity, or rather falsely. Ex. xxiii. 1. Deut. v. 11.

15.text: Opposite. Or equal. Gr. "clothed with death." He denotes blasphemy, (Lev. xxiv. 14.) or the invitation to idolatry, (Deut. xiii. 1.) or calumny. v. 17. Lev. xix. 12. C. --- In oaths God is called to witness, as being unable to deceive. But blasphemy attributes to him or to others what does not belong to them. W.

16.text: Merciful. Or true believers, Assideans. 1 Mac. ii. 42.

17.text: Of sin. A Hebrew idiom, to imply something criminal. Those who have laid aside shame, are capable of any wickedness.

18.text: Men. Treat thy parents with no less regard, (C.) even though thou shouldst be exalted in dignity. Lyr. ---Thus thou wilt be rewarded, (C.) of if thou transgress, wilt be brought to judgment. Bossuet. --- Gr. "thou shalt sit," &c. H.

19.text: Nativity. Wish not that thou hadst not been born of such parents. Grot.

20.text: Life. For who will admonish him?

21.text: Two. The first is a passionate man, (v. 22.) the second a libertine, (v. 23.) and the third an adulterer. v. 25. C.

22.text: Hot. With any furious passion, (Vat.) or anger, (C.) avarice, (W.) or lust. M.

23.text: Mouth. Gr. "body." --- Fire. Shameful disease will come upon him. C. xix. 3. His brutal passion will never be satiated. C.

24.text: Sweet. He is not delicate in his choice. H. --- All obstacles increase his irregular desires. Prov. ix. 17. C.

27.text: And. Gr. "the eyes of men are his dread." H. --- Such is the folly of the adulterer!

30.text: And he. Gr. "and where," &c. He shall be stoned. Lev. xx. 10. C. --- Taken. Gr. subjoins (v. 32.) "so," &c. H. --- If carnal adultery be thus punished, how much more will spiritual adultery, schism, and apostacy from the Catholic religion? W.

38.text: Shall. Gr. "that thou shouldst be taken under his protection." H.
